newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Q3 GDP up 1.0 pct vs previous quarter.
newsitem.headline: German Q3 GDP up 1.0 pct vs previous quarter.

text.p: Germany's economy expanded by one percent in the third quarter after a 1.5 percent increase in the previous quarter, data showed on Wednesday, putting growth at the top end of analysts expectations.
Year-on-year growth in pan-German gross domestic product (GDP) dubled its pace in the third quarter to 2.4 percent from 1.2 percent, the Federal Statistics Office said.
Both GDP numbers were at the top of market expectations.
"It's a touch stronger than people expected. It's probably within the overall range of expectations," Rob Hayward at Bank of America said.
Analysts said they expected the recovery to tail off in the fourth quarter and into 1997, still leaving scope for a possible further easing of short-term interest rates by the Bundesbank.
"This is a look into the rear mirror and ahead of us appears to be a rather flat fourth quarter," Adolf Rosenstock at the Industrial Bank of Japan said of the data.

Following the release of disappointing October industrial data "you would need a tremendous increase in November and December just to break even on the third quarter," Rosenstock said. He added that the outlook for 1997 was "still muted".
Rosenstock said an easing of the repo rate could come towards the end of January. But Juergen Pfister of Commerzbank ruled out any further rate reductions.
"It's quite clear that the economy is on an upward path but a slow one," Pfister said.

"We don't see any possibility for a further cut in short-term interest rates as all the Bundesbank's arguments for lower rates -- a weak economy and a stronger mark -- are no longer there," Pfister added.

Analysts said there might be a slight correction to the German bond market's rally, but the overall trend towards lower yields would remain intact. The weaker tone of the mark against the dollar was likely to continue, they said.
